podcast.title: Drifters-Sounding Name (Lover Patterson Management)
podcast.body: The Drapers were a group managed by Lover Patterson, who was also Benny King's manager. The group was intentionally given a name that sounded as similar to "The Drifters" as possible, suggesting an attempt to capitalize on their recognition. "The drapers, the group they joined, was managed by Lever Patterson, Benny Kingsmanager, and had been given a name that sounded as much like the drifters as possible."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 94: "Stand By Me", by Ben E. King

podcast.title: Members from Drifters Lineup
podcast.body: The Drapers included Doc Green and Tommy Evans, who were both members of The Drifters, as well as Johnny Moore and Carnation Charlie Hughes, who had been in the same 1956 lineup of The Drifters that Tommy Evans had been in. "As well as Green and Evans, it also had Johnny Moore and Carnation Charlie Hughes, who had been in the same 1956 lineup of the drifters that Tommy Evans had been in."

podcast.title: One Single Release
podcast.body: This lineup of The Drapers released only one single, which did not perform particularly well commercially. "That lineup of the drapers released one single that didn't do particularly well."
